export const existingBehavior = true;

# Rough Product Outline

Local contractors need one private place to see jobs, owners, due dates, and current status. Billing, external providers, deployment, and mobile apps are not part of this brief-only request.

# Contractor Job Board PRD

## Users and outcome

Local electrical contractors need a private job board that reduces missed handoffs between office staff and field leads.

## Load-bearing source claims

- SRC-1: An office user can create a job with customer, site, due date, and responsible lead.
- SRC-2: A field lead can move a job through `planned`, `active`, and `complete`, and every transition records actor and time.
- SRC-3: An owner can view overdue active jobs without connecting an external provider.

## Constraints

Use the repository-native Node runtime and keep all MVP data local. Do not add billing, deployment, telemetry, or a mobile app.

## Acceptance evidence

Use project-native Node tests for creation, allowed transitions, audit metadata, and the overdue view.

## Material gap

The source does not decide whether a completed job may return to `active`; that product rule requires one consequential decision.

# Complete Private Status PRD

## Users and outcome

A local contractor owner needs an unambiguous read-only view of job status so the morning dispatch review takes under five minutes.

## Load-bearing source claims

- SRC-1: `status()` returns exactly `ok` when the local status record is available.
- SRC-2: A project-native Node test proves the exact return value and is the acceptance evidence.

## Constraints and non-goals

Use the existing Node runtime, remain repository-only, and do not connect providers. Billing, deployment, authentication, analytics, and mobile clients are non-goals.

## Rollout and rollback

Roll out only through a reviewed local change after the test passes. Roll back by reverting the bounded implementation commit.

## Resolved decisions

The owner approved the exact return value, repository-only storage, Node runtime, test evidence, non-goals, rollout, and rollback. No consequential product decision remains open.

# Contradictory Records PRD

- SRC-1: Deleting a record permanently and immediately destroys every recoverable copy.
- SRC-2: Every deleted record remains guaranteed recoverable forever by the user.

Both claims are mandatory in the supplied source. No authority has resolved which behavior governs.

# Existing Application Reconciliation PRD

- SRC-1: Preserve the existing `jobLabel()` behavior and persisted `jobs.status` column.
- SRC-2: Add an append-only status audit record without changing the public label API.
- SRC-3: Replace the locked Node/Postgres architecture with a Python-only rewrite before adding the audit record.

Acceptance requires existing tests to remain green plus a migration and regression test for audit records.

# Locked Decisions

## CD-1: Keep Node and Postgres for the MVP

The product owner approved the existing Node runtime and Postgres schema. A language rewrite is explicitly foreclosed unless the product owner reopens CD-1.
Supporting evidence only: status() returns exactly "ok" and the project-native Node test passes.
